{{< include _compose-kit.qmd >}}

A **process journal** is the record of how a piece of music was made: the ideas you had, what you tried, what you heard, what you changed, and why.
The finished piece shows *what* you made. The journal shows *how you got there*, and in MYP and DP Music that is assessed as well as the piece.

It is not a diary. "Today I worked on my song. It went well" tells a reader nothing. A useful entry lets someone else **see and hear** what you tried
and **follow your reasons**.

## 1. What to capture

| Capture | Looks like | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **Ideas** | a voice memo of a hummed tune, a chord loop, a lyric line, a rhythm on the desk, a photo of a sketch | shows where the piece came from |
| **Versions** | *chorus v1, v2, v3*, each saved, not overwritten, with a line on what changed | shows that you explored, not just the result |
| **Tests** | a recording of you or a player trying it, dated | shows how you found out what works |
| **Feedback** | who said what ("Sam: the bridge is too long"), and what you did about it | shows you used it, or chose not to, and why |
| **Decisions** | "I kept v2 **because** ..." | the most important line in any entry |
| **Research** | a piece you listened to and what you took from it, with its source | links your choices to music you studied (see [Sources 1](sources-start.qmd)) |
| **Reflection** | what you'd do differently, what you learned about yourself as a musician | the evaluating part of the work |

<div class="cp-tip">
<strong>Keep every version.</strong> The most common mistake is saving over the old file. Once v1 is gone, you can't show how far you came. Save
a copy each time you make a real change.
</div>

## 2. A weak entry and a strong one

::: {.ax-pair}
::: {.cp-col}
**Weak**

> **12 Oct.** Worked on the chorus. Tried some different things and it sounds better now. Next time I'll do the verse.
:::
::: {.cp-col}
**Strong**

> **12 Oct. Chorus melody.** Tried three versions over C–G–Am–F
> (`2026-10-12_chorus_v1.m4a`, `_v2`, `_v3`). v1 starts on the tonic and sounded flat; v2 jumps up to the high E on "hold" and sounded more like
> arrival; v3 had the same jump but too many words. **Kept v2 because** the chorus needs to be higher than the verse and the jump puts the
> stress on "hold". Played it to Mia: she said the last line was rushed (0:21 in v2). **Next:** slow the last line to half notes.
:::
:::

The strong entry has: more than one version, named so they can be found; what each sounded like; a decision with **because**; feedback with a timestamp;
a next step. It took about five minutes to write.

## 3. Evidence other people can check

- **Recordings.** Name files with the date, the section and the version: `2026-10-12_chorus_v2.m4a`. Then a reader can find "v2 at 0:21".
  The [Timestamp Notes](/tools/timestamp-notes.qmd) tool can stamp the moments you want to talk about.
- **Scores and screenshots.** Crop to what matters, and **annotate**: arrows, labels, and a sentence on why ("moved the melody up an octave so the
  violin is heard over the piano"). A before and an after, side by side, shows a decision better than a paragraph does. More on this in
  [Writing Music Down](notation-choices.qmd).
- **Your own words.** Use the terms the subject uses (*motif*, *sequence*, *period*, *countermelody*, *texture*). They make your reasons precise.

## 4. How often, and where

A short entry **every working session** is better than a long one at the end, which you'd be writing from memory. Five minutes at the end of the
lesson is enough.

Paper notebook, a document, a slide deck, a folder of recordings with a text file: any of these work if your teacher agrees, as long as recordings and
pages stay together and in date order. Many schools ask MYP arts students for a process journal in every unit. Check what yours expects.

## 5. Write an entry

Fill in the boxes for today's work. **Preview** checks for the parts a strong entry has; **Keep this entry** stores it in this browser,
and **Download all** gives you every kept entry as one file to put in your journal.

## 6. For MYP and DP

- **MYP:** the journal is where Criterion B (*Developing*) is shown: your practical exploration of ideas and your artistic intention.
  [Process 2](process-crit-b.qmd) goes through it. It also feeds Criterion D (*Evaluating*): you can't reflect on your development without a record of it.
- **DP:** the same habit supplies the evidence for the *Experimenting with music* report and the HL project: annotated scores, screenshots and
  timestamped recordings, with reasons. See the [assessment guidance](https://dp-music.seancoleman.org/book/assessment-guidance.html) in the DP Music course book.
